newsitem.title: USA: Privacy lawsuit against Metromail widened.
newsitem.headline: Privacy lawsuit against Metromail widened.

text.p: A privacy violation lawsuit brought by an Ohio grandmother against Metromail Corp, a marketing database provider, has been amended to include three other plaintiffs, the law firm that filed the case said Monday.

The amended lawsuit, which is seeking class-action status, now includes a plaintiff each from California, Illinois and New York, according to Mike Lenett, of the Washington, D.C.-based law firm of Cuneo Law Group P.C., the plaintiffs' lawyers.
Lenett said the plaintiffs, all of whom allegedly completed consumer survey questionnaires from Metromail, are seeking unspecified amounts in damages.

Lombard, Ill.,-based Metromail was spun off from R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co in June last year. Donnelley, a large commercial printer based in Chicago, is also named in the lawsuit. A Donnelley spokesman referred requests for comment to Metromail.
The lawsuit alleges it is wrongful for the defendants to use Texas prison facilities to process personal and private information of consumers without their knowledge or consent.
The law firm filed the original complaint in the case before a state court in Texas on behalf of Beverly Dennis a year ago.

Dennis had alleged that she completed a Metromail consumer survey, thinking she would receive product samples. Instead, she allegedly received "a highly offensive, sexually graphic and threatening letter" from an inmate at the data processing work program hired through a Metromail subcontractor at the Wynne prison at Hunstville, Texas.
Metromail spokesman Tim Fitzpatrick said that the prisoner had memorized data from Dennis' survey form.
Fitzpatrick said Metromail maintains the incident was "extremely unusual" and "unfortunate," and had ordered the subcontractor to terminate the contract with Texas prison authorities.
Metromail is now implementing a policy banning the use of prisons for processing data, he said.
The Texas Department of Criminal Justice and its representative, who were named in the original lawsuit, had been discharged from the case earlier this month, according to Fitzpatrick and Lenett.
"Metromail is fully confident that this lawsuit will not be certified as a class action suit," Fitzpatrick said.
